title: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitutions of Aniline & Protection Strategies
topics: Direct Bromination: Reaction with Bromine Water (Br₂/H₂O) yielding 2,4,6-Tribromoaniline (White Precipitate)
Protection Strategy: Acetylation with Acetic Anhydride in Pyridine to form Acetanilide (Ph-NHCOCH₃)
Mechanism of Protection: Lone Pair Delocalization into Amide Carbonyl Moderating Ring Activation
Regioselective Synthesis of 4-Bromoaniline via Protected Intermediate & Acid Hydrolysis
quickSummary: The -NH₂ group in aniline is so strongly activating that reaction with bromine water causes complete polybromination to 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (white ppt). To obtain monobromo derivatives, the -NH₂ group is protected by acetylation with acetic anhydride to Acetanilide (Ph-NHCOCH₃), which moderates ring activation by delocalizing nitrogen lone pair into the carbonyl.
summary: Master aniline ring activation, polybromination behavior, and acetylation protection protocols.

summaryBox.takeaway: Bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline white ppt. To prepare p-bromoaniline, protect -NH₂ as acetanilide (Ph-NHCOCH₃), brominate, then hydrolyze.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ANILINE PROTECTION & REGIOSELECTIVITY
                        
   Direct Bromination ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) ──► **2,4,6-Tribromoaniline \downarrow (White Precipitate)**
   
   PROTECTION ROUTE (To prepare $p$-monobromoaniline):
   $\text{Ph-NH}_2 \xrightarrow{(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O} / \text{Pyridine}} \mathbf{\text{Ph-NHCOCH}_3 \text{ (Acetanilide)}} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{AcOH}} \text{4-Bromoacetanilide} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \mathbf{\text{4-Bromoaniline}}$
conceptBreakdown.content: Due to the intense $+M$ activation of $-	ext{NH}_2$, direct bromination with $	ext{Br}_2/	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$ yields $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline. Acetylation converts $-	ext{NH}_2$ into $-	ext{NHCOCH}_3$, where the lone pair is resonance-delocalized into the carbonyl oxygen, moderating activation to allow clean mono-substitution.
